trace.msg: Let's look at this puzzle carefully. I'll only move when I can explain why.
I can't rule out left or down yet, so I'll make an educated guess: left.

Contradiction! Every way forward fails: going up leaves no safe move afterwards; going down would force the two-exit cells to link up into a loop (or put the numbers out of order). So my guess (left from number 1) was wrong, so the line must go down.
I can't rule out down or left yet, so I'll make an educated guess: down.

Contradiction! Every way forward fails: going left, the next 3 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (5,2); going right, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So my guess (down from cell (5,3)) was wrong, so the line must go left.
Going down would leave both cell (6,1) and cell (6,3) needing the line next, and it can't do both; going up, the next move is forced and the line gets stuck at cell (3,2). So the line goes left.

Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes right.
